News.title: Girl, 11, dies after hair gets caught in swimming pool’s drain during family holiday in Italy
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

POOL HORROR Girl, 11, dies after hair gets caught in swimming pool’s drain during family holiday in Italy

AN eleven-year-old girl has died after her hair got caught in a swimming pool drain.

The young girl, named Alice, was on a family holiday in the beach town of Sestri Levante, Italy when tragedy struck.



She had travelled south from Milan for a sunny getaway with her mum.

The duo were at the same beach resort on the tourist town’s Descalzo promenade that they had stayed at several years in a row.



The horror incident happened in the indoor pool, where the water is cooler than the sea.

But despite the shallow water, her hair got stuck in the pool’s drain.

The force dragged Alice under water and was trapped.

Onlookers desperately tried to pull her out but struggled to disentangle her hair from the drain.

An ambulance rushed to the scene and paramedics attempted CPR.

She was taken by helicopter to hospital in nearby Genoa and put in intensive care in critical condition.



Tragically, she was pronounced dead in hospital.

Police are investigating the death and attended the scene.

Investigators are considering if swimming caps should be mandatory to swim in the shallow pool.

Alice is the fifth child to die in an Italian pool in just three months as experts warn of “death trap” drains.

Italian Minister for Civil Protection Nello Musumeci said: “Strict discipline is needed, but also greater caution is needed in never leaving children alone in the water.



“The Meloni government’s bill, aimed at this goal, will be approved by the relevant committee within the month, and we will do everything possible to schedule it urgently.”

In April, Gabriele Petrucci, seven, was celebrating his birthday when he was found unresponsive in the water.

The boy “fought like a lion” after getting trapped in a hotel swimming pool’s suction duct at a wellness retreat in Castelforte.

His dad dived in to try desperately to save him but Gabriele sadly died.

News.title: Paranoid Putin’s goons arrest pro-regime propagandist in his underwear after he turned on tyrant & forecast Kremlin coup
News.content:
A PRO-KREMLIN propagandist who turned on Vladimir Putin and forecast a coup to oust him was dramatically arrested in Russia today.

Paranoid Putin’s goons detained Ilya Remeslo, 42, in his underwear at his St Petersburg home just hours after he stepped up his public criticism of the Kremlin dictator.



In a post on Thursday he told followers: “I believe everything is going according to plan, toward a change in the old Russian leadership this year.

“The situation is rapidly deteriorating for Putin.”



Ilya claimed the spiralling energy crisis caused by Ukrainian drones smashing oil refineries and depots in the heart of Russia was speeding up Putin’s demise.

Fuel shortages have sparked chaos across the country with queues triggering petrol pump fights and brawling.

And Ilya said unrest within the Russian ruling circle was “intensifying”.

“Everything is moving toward a situation where even a small push could lead to Putin losing power,” he said.

“I am able to say that Putin will be led away by the arms this autumn.”

Ilya is rumoured to be speaking with the support of elements of the Russian security services.



He was transported to Moscow and is expected to face charges linked to his criticism of the war.

The former Kremlin supporter could face up to ten years in jail for “spreading false information about the armed forces” – a catch-all crime that has been ruthlessly used against foes of Putin.

His lawyer Sergei Badamshin told Russian news agency TASS that Ilya’s home had been searched.



“A decision on pretrial detention for Remeslo will be made soon,” the lawyer said.

Ilya positioned himself as a loyalist who had turned against Putin and was ready to lead the opposition to build a new Russia.

“I am the person who knows how to fight Vladimir Putin, who knows the system’s weaknesses, how to interact with it, and how to lure people out of it”: he previously declared.

Putin’s inner circle “secretly hate” him and the dictator will be toppled in a “palace coup”.

“It will be something very quiet. You know, like what happened in 1953 [when Stalin died and was replaced by Nikita Khrushchev].



Who is Ilya Remeslo? ILYA Remeslo is a 42-year-old pro-Kremlin lawyer and firm supporter of the Russian regime. He broke ranks earlier this week by calling out Vladimir Putin and demanding that the tyrant be overthrown. The popular Z-blogger was previously involved in tearing down Alexei Navalny’s opposition campaign against Putin. Remeslo even appeared in court proceedings against Navalny before the opposition figure was poisoned and died. Remeslo lives in St Petersburg where he studied law in 2005. He was a member of Russia’s Kremlin-backed Public Chamber , meaning he was working for Moscow. The influencer has been accused of spewing pro-Kremlin propaganda and denouncing opponents of the regime. He has consistently peddled pro-Putin lines relating to the war in Ukraine.

“We’ll wake up in a different country,” he said.

An extraordinary surge of pessimism about Russia’s war in Ukraine has engulfed Putin’s staunch allies.

And as rumours of Putin’s downfall continue to swirl, the Kremlin leader has fled into hiding – reportedly cowering in bunkers for weeks at a time.

Earlier this year Ilya was sent – in Soviet-style – to a psychiatric clinic after his scathing criticisms of Putin.



He was quickly released but continued his campaign against the tyrant.

“Putin is not a legitimate president,” he said.

“Vladimir Putin must resign and be prosecuted as a war criminal and a thief.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Another Putin foe Boris Nadezhin, 63, was this week accused of “extremism,” a tactic to stop him standing in parliamentary elections in September.

He was also banned from leaving Russia.

News.title: Solicitor suing RSPCA after cops ‘chopped through front door with axe & shoved her to ground to seize disabled cat’
News.content:
MOGGED OFF Solicitor suing RSPCA after cops ‘chopped through front door with axe & shoved her to ground to seize disabled cat’

A SOLICITOR is suing the RSPCA after police allegedly chopped through her front door with an axe to seize her disabled cat.

Dr Katherine Theodotou claims she was “pushed violently to the ground” during a raid by six cops and two RSPCA officers.



Her cat Rita was taken away from the home in North London following a report she was being mistreated.

Dr Theodotou – former human rights lawyer of the year – insists she was the victim of a “malicious report” to the RSPCA.



The 79-year-old is suing both the RSPCA and the Commissioner of the Metropolitan Police, asking for an order that her cat be returned by the RSPCA, as well as an award of damages.

But lawyers for the RSPCA claim they acted in Rita’s “best interests” after receiving a report from vets that indicated her condition had deteriorated under Dr Theodotou’s care.



The High Court was told the moggy was born disabled and cannot properly move her back legs – meaning she suffers from occasional infections in her bladder.

Dr Theodotou claims she pampers Rita and spends large sums of money keeping her “safe and well” – including paying for two private nurses and a personal physiotherapist for her.

Her solicitor Liam Wells said: “Dr Theodotou knows Rita to be an intelligent cat and knows that Rita has been steadily learning to walk on all four legs.

“She says that prior to April 2025 Rita was being well cared for by her at her home and Rita received regular medical support from specialist veterinary surgeons paid for by her.”



The court heard Rita had been cared for by vets for several months during 2025 before being returned to her owner’s care, after which two RSPCA inspections uncovered no issues.

But following the alleged “malicious report” to the RSPCA over the cat’s welfare, a warrant was obtained that gave officers permission to raid Dr Theodotou’s home and seize Rita.

Mr Wells said: “On 27 March 2026, Dr Theodotou was at the private dwelling at the property with Rita and was recovering from her recent bilateral breast cancer surgery.



“It was a complete surprise when the RSPCA attended the property accompanied by six officers of the Metropolitan Police.

“Dr Theodotou did not understand the reasons for the attendance of so many uniformed police officers at the property and did not wish to allow them access.

“The officers of the Metropolitan Police proceeded to break down the front door to the property using an axe.”

The court was told Dr Theodotou had gone to open the door but was “pushed violently to the ground, making forceful contact with her wounded chest”.

Rita was then removed from the property and is yet to be returned to her owner.



Lawyers for Dr Theodotou are now asking for an emergency interim injunction to ward off any danger of her cat being put down before the case comes to trial.

Mr Wells added: “Rita is amongst the most well cared for cats you could find. My client is spending large sums of money on keeping her safe and well and teaching her to walk again.

“Both parties want what is in the best interest of Rita. From my client’s perspective, euthanasia is not in Rita’s best interests.”

But RSPCA barrister Mark Townsend however told the judge that when Rita was seized, a physical exam revealed her overall condition was “extremely concerning and consistent with a significant deterioration since discharge”.

He claimed there was evidence that suggested “prolonged inadequate hygiene, nursing care, and monitoring within the home environment”.



Mr Townsend said the cat was put in a veterinary hospital and “is currently doing well” with foster carers.

He added: “She has flourished once again and has developed a ‘wonderfully loving, cheeky temperament.

“Rita’s health conditions are complex, but with the daily care and treatment she is receiving, she is progressing very well, and there is no intention to euthanise her.”

Dr Theodotou was struck off the UK solicitors register in 2022 after she was found to have made “dishonest” statements while applying for professional insurance.

She is also the founder and honorary director of the Greek school of Islington and runs an animal sanctuary at Woodcock Lodge Farm, near Hertford.



The former solicitor is seeking damages for harassment and or negligence against the RSPCA and damages for assault, battery, trespass and negligence against the Metropolitan Police.

Ruling against her application for an interim injunction banning the cat being put down, Ms Justice Obi said: “I am not satisfied that there is a real or imminent risk of euthanasia.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The application was adjourned until a magistrates court hearing later this month where the RSPCA are seeking to take legal possession of Rita.

Dr Theodotou’s case for damages and for the cat to be returned is being pursued in the High Court and will return at a later date, unless the parties can reach an out of court agreement.

News.title: Can I report my neighbour if their BBQ smoke fills my garden? Your legal rights explained
News.content:
SUMMER weather often means more BBQs, but heavy smoke can cause some tension between neighbours leaving many unsure of their rights.

Even the friendliest of neighbours can find themselves in a tense dispute over BBQ smoke during the summer months.

While disputes commonly happen over garden fences, parking spaces and the like, BBQ smoke ruining outside washing, seeping into homes and causing breathing issues can sour relationships quickly.



But what you can do about a neighbour being inconsiderate is quite limited, from a legal standpoint.



There is no outright law in the UK banning BBQs in gardens or private outdoor spaces, even when it is annoying.

With that said, excessive smoke, fumes or repeated disturbances could amount to what councils call “statutory nuisance” in some circumstances.

Islington Council has previously warned that nuisances could result in court appearances and a hefty fine if convicted.

Councils will typically issue warnings first and will consider factors such as frequency, duration and severity if a complaint has been lodged by a neighbour.

Under GOV.UK guidance, local authorities can investigate complaints involving smoke, fumes and smells that unreasonably interfere with somebody’s use or enjoyment of their property.

While individuals are encouraged to try and resolve the problem with the neighbour civilly, if issues persist, there are steps they can take that can help bolster their complaint.

Citizens Advice suggests residents should keep a written record detailing dates, times and the impact on their property and well being.



Evidence such as photographs, videos or diary logs can also help support complaints if disputes continue.

News.title: Burnham insists ‘I have a plan’ as he takes over as Labour leader amid criticism he has failed to outline ANY agenda
News.content:
ANDY Burnham insisted “I have a plan” for Britain as he formally took over as Labour leader today.

The incoming PM, who will enter No10 on Monday, dismissed criticism he had failed to spell out a proper blueprint for government.



As he took over the party reins from Sir Keir Starmer, he said he was “ready” for the top job and would “do politics differently”.

He has provided few details of what he will do differently from the outgoing Prime Minister.



In his speech today, Mr Burnham promised that he had a clear plan for the country.

He said: “I have a plan. And what I also want you to know is that I want change. I have a style, it’s my style.



“I will always stay close to the ground. Close to the people.

“I will always stay the same because I draw my strength from people, I hear things, pick up straws in the wind as I was going about Manchester as my job as mayor.”

The former Greater Manchester mayor will become the UK’s seventh Prime Minister in 10 years on Monday.

It marks a remarkable rise from becoming an MP in June to the PM-in-waiting a month later.



Mr Burnham was backed by 379 Labour MPs after emerging as the only candidate to stand for the party leadership.

However, he will not officially become Prime Minister until Monday.

Next week Sir Keir will travel to see the King at Buckingham Palace, where he will offer his resignation as Prime Minister.

Mr Burnham will then hold a private audience with the King, who will formally appoint him as PM.

Sir Keir lasted for just over two years as Prime Minister having won a landslide majority at the 2024 general election.



Now Mr Burnham will inherit an intray from hell including sluggish growth, a small boats crisis, global conflict in Ukraine and the Middle East.

His team have had just weeks to come up with a slew of policies to help hard-up Brits with the cost of living and sky-high energy bills.

What will Andy Burnham's 'New Order' look like? By Ryan Sabey Andy Burnham may not have put much meat on the bones of policy but he offered plenty of “hope”. The incoming PM wants to govern distinctivly as Labour by giving hope back to the British people. Perhaps he is the right person to make it happen. His warm-up music before he took to the stage, after all, was the Blossoms’ Perfect Me! But hope sadly doesn’t pay the bills or put petrol in the car but he insists he has a plan of action. The ex-Greater Manchester mayor has now formally been named Labour leader before he heads into Downing Street on Monday. Labour members, trade union bosses and MPs all joined him in central London to mark the moment. It didn’t take long for him to take aim at ex-Tory PM Margaret Thatcher. He said the country had taken a “series of wrong turns” in the 1980s and he comes to power trying to fix it. He took a swipe at Reform leader Nigel Farage in his thirty-nine address. He told his party they can’t take on the “new right” if they are pulling in different directions. Green leader Zak Polanski also came under attack. Mr Burnham promised that he wouldn’t “out Green the Greens or out Reform, Reform”. He made great play of this moment in Britain as the last chance to change. He’s an untested politician who talks of hope and getting growth in every postcode. But all that can go by the wayside while confronting President Xi, or Trump on the world stage. As he walked off the stage to one of his favourite bands, he’s really got a long way to go if this really is going to be a New Order.

At the Labour conference today, Mr Burnham said: “If we want an economy and a country that works for all people and places which to me should always be at the very core of Labourism, then it requires a new path to the one we’ve been on for the last 40 years.

“The Government I lead will confidently lay that path out, starting next week, and that is why this change today is the most significant change moment in our politics for 40 years.

“It will take us to a country where life is more affordable, and all people and places are lifted from where they are now.”



His wife Marie-France van Heel, who Mr Burnham met at university, was watching on as he made his speech.

Mr Burnham committed to being a leader “for the North and the South, for Scotland, for Wales and for Northern Ireland, and for every town and every city in every nation and region of this great country”.

He added: “I mean it when I say all places. I will be a leader for the north, the south, the east and the west, for Scotland, Wales and for Northern Ireland.

“Yes, the north of England has given me so much, everything, in fact. And in return I have sought to give it the strongest voice I could. That was my job. But now I do the same for everywhere.”

He said that Labour must “lift Britain up” by putting people at the heart of national decision-making.



The new Labour leader will argue that “Britain took a series of wrong turns in the 1980s” when “political power was centralised and economic power privatised”.

He said: “The Right use the phrase ‘take back control’ but they are the ones who gave it away in the first place”.

Mr Burnham promised to be a pro-business leader of the Labour party, claiming he will continue in the same vein as he did as Manchester mayor.

But he promised to do this in an unashamedly Labour way.

He added: “If we want an economy and a country that works for all people and places which to me should always be at the very core of Labourism, then it requires a new path to the one we’ve been on for the last 40 years.



“The Government I lead will confidently lay that path out, starting next week, and that is why this change today is the most significant change moment in our politics for 40 years.”

Mr Burnham has largely avoided scrutiny from the press, having conducted just one media interview since returning to Westminster.

He has opted to answer questions on Reddit forums and take selected questions from the public.

Mr Burnham said he was ready to build on the foundations of Sir Keir’s leader.

Many Labour MPs are starting to become increasingly worried over who could be the next Chancellor.



Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood, who is on the right of the party, is set to take over the reins in the Treasury.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Last month Mr Burnham won a crunch Makerfield by-election, which set him on course to challenge Sir Keir as Prime Minister.

Mr Burnham secured 24,927 votes and won by a majority of 9,231 – which returned him to Westminster for the first time in nine years.

News.title: Innocent mum ‘with heart of gold’ killed by driver as he fled cops in horror hit-and-run smash
News.content:
DEATH CRASH Innocent mum ‘with heart of gold’ killed by driver as he fled cops in horror hit-and-run smash

A MUM “with heart of gold” was killed in a horror hit-and-run smash during a police chase with young driver.

Lydia La Polla, 47, was driving in a Toyota with her 16-year-old son and husband when she was hit by a silver Mercedes being pursued by the police.



The collision happened shortly after 9:30pm on March 24, 2025 between Belgrave Road and Percy Road in Hightown, Wrexham, North Wales.

The “selfless” mum from Wrexham died in hospital two days later while a police hunt was launched to find the killer and his passenger.



Her husband and 16-year-old, were also seriously injured.

Pathologist of Royal Stoke University Hospital declared at her inquest that the cause of death was a severe blunt force head injury as a result of the crash.

Michael Connors, 28, from Dublin, was eventually arrested on March 11, 2026, and extradited back to the UK three months later.

Connors appeared at Mold Crown Court via video link on July 17, where he admitted three charges in relation to the incident.

He pleaded guilty to causing death by dangerous driving and two charges of causing serious injury by dangerous driving.

The case was adjourned for a pre-sentence report to determine Connors’ level of risk to the public.



District Judge MC Jones told Connors in court: “I’m sure you will understand that in view of the nature of the charges that you have admitted today the starting point is a significant custodial sentence.”

At the time of her death, her family told Wales News: “Lydia had a true heart of gold and would always be there for others with her selfless acts of kindness.

“She was devoted to her family and friends.

“The night of Monday 24 March has scarred us for the rest of our lives. Life will never be the same without her.”

Chief Superintendent Jaqueline Downes said: “Our deepest sympathies remain with the family of Lydia La Polla following their tragic loss.



“We will continue to support them through each stage of the investigation and upcoming court proceedings.

“As this remains an active investigation, it is important that people do not speculate about the incident online.”

News.title: Toddler killed by TikTok-watching driver, 32, who smashed into back of car at roundabout
News.content:
CRASH TRAGEDY Toddler killed by TikTok-watching driver, 32, who smashed into back of car at roundabout

A TODDLER was killed after a driver who was watching Tiktok videos ploughed into the back of his mum’s car.

Chloe Baker was travelling home from an after school club with her son, Finley, when Hristo Iliev’s car smashed into hers and left the 20-month-old unresponsive.



The tot was raced to hospital with life-threatening injuries and died two days later.

The Bulgarian national was looking at clips on Tiktok when he hit Chloe’s car at the Holdingham roundabout on the A17, Lincolnshire, on 19 March last year.



He approached a queue of slow-moving traffic in his Volkswagon Passat but failed to react.

His car ploughed into Chloe’s stationary Kia Ceed and shunted her car into the Audi A5 in front.



Chloe, Finley and her other 8-year-old son who was in the back of the car were rushed to hospital.

The mum has since had a major reconstructive surgery after her shoulder was injured in the crash.

Iliev, of Hide Close, Boston, Lincolnshire, was found to have been using Tiktok and Apple TV for seven minutes before the smash.

A police spokesperson said: “Evidence of video viewing, uploading and downloading was evident.



“Crucially in the moments before the collision occurred, the examination found that the TikTok application was in use and a video was playing.”

He was jailed for 11 years and three months at Lincoln Crown Court on 11 June, after previously admitting to causing death by dangerous driving.

A heartbreaking tribute has now been released by Finley’s parents Chloe and Daniel for their “a little ray of sunshine”.

They said: “As Finley grew, he became kind, loving, curious and brought joy to everyone he met and everywhere he went. He had the most beautiful smile and his bright blue eyes would light up the room.”

The couple said he filled the family home with fun and laughter.



He loved dancing with his brother, reading book, riding his bike and meeting dogs when they went for walks, they added.

Finley’s mum and dad said: “Appalling choices made the day we lost Finley mean we never get to hear his little voice again.”

“We don’t get to take him to his first day of school, watch him in his first school nativity or sports day.”

They added a “Finley shaped hole” had been left after “his entire life was stolen from him for the most senseless of reasons.

“No parent should ever have to outlive their child, let alone lose them in the most horrific way like we did.



“It splits your life into two, the before and the after and we wouldn’t wish for anyone to live in this after.”

Daniel and Chloe said: “Knowing how full of life he was and how much he still had to experience in life, makes his death impossible to accept.

“We will forever continue to honour and remember him for the beautiful little soul that he was.”

Daniel and Chloe thanked the members of the public that stopped and helped them after the horrific crash and Lincolnshire Police for their support over the last 15 months.

Detective Sergeant James Perring, from the Serious Collision Investigation Unit, said: “This collision was due to the dangerous driving of Iliev when he selfishly paid no attention to his driving as he watched videos on his devices.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Those actions cost a young toddler his life and seriously injured another, destroying lives in a way which can never be undone.

“The importance of concentration and not being distracted cannot be overstated. This was a wholly preventable collision, and I feel nothing but disappointment for the way he has so pointlessly destroyed lives. I would implore anybody thinking of behaving in the same way never to do so.”

News.title: Hospital warns 'this is why' after fire caused by patient's vape
News.content:
Hospital warns 'this is why' after fire caused by patient's vape

'It was a really scary moment... I was covered in smoke and terrified'

View 3 Images The unnamed woman was engulfed in flames after she began using her e-cigarette device while connected to an oxygen supply (Image: South Tyneside and Sunderland NHS Foundation Trust © SWNS)

A patient accidentally set her own head 'on fire' after making a nightmare mistake in her hospital bed. The incident has prompted the hospital to issue a warning to millions who vape. The woman, who has not been named, lit up her vape while hooked to an oxygen supply at Sunderland Royal Hospital. It was these oxygen-fed flames that rapidly tore through the hospital bed in a terrifying flash.

‌



Hero nurse Emmanuel Ndubuisi didn’t hesitate, charging in through the smoke to shut off the oxygen and put out the fire with an extinguisher. The patient suffered burns to her head and needed treatment, but the quick response stopped it from becoming even more serious.

‌



The aftermath photos show just how fierce the blaze was inside the ward. Emmanuel has now earned a national bravery honour for his actions during the incident last August.

‌



He said: "On the day, it was a really scary moment, and you never know how you're going to initially react. It was all about teamwork and everyone acted so quickly.

"I was covered in smoke and terrified. It's a real honour and motivates me to keep doing my best for our patients and colleagues every day." He was presented with a Cavell Star Award for staying calm under pressure and protecting others in the moments after the fire broke out.

View 3 Images A vape caused the fire, which tore through the room in a terrifying flash (Image: Getty)

‌



Karen Sheard, the hospital’s director of nursing, midwifery and allied health professionals, said: "This is a powerful example of our Trust’s values in action. In the NHS, we often talk about our values – compassion, respect, teamwork and honesty, but this is about seeing those values lived in practice.

"Emmanuel represents the very best of our profession, reminds us why we are proud to work in healthcare and inspires all of us to continue striving for excellence." She said: "Thank you for all you do. We are incredibly proud to have Emmanual part of our team."

After the scare, bosses at South Tyneside and Sunderland NHS Foundation Trust renewed warnings over vaping and smoking inside hospitals. Jim Charlton, the hospital's fire safety and security manager, said: "This shocking incident shows exactly why we ask our patients and visitors not to vape inside our buildings. We do that to keep everyone safe.

‌



View 3 Images Emmanuel Ndubuisi with his Cavell Star Award (Image: South Tyneside and Sunderland NHS Foundation Trust © SWNS)

"Our staff should be able to work without fear of the damage and risk vapes and cigarettes cause. The staff on the ward where this incident happened are to be commended on their swift response.

"They turned off the oxygen and put out the fire with an extinguisher. All of those involved were fantastic." He added: "We will continue to remind patients and visitors about the fire risk of both vapes and cigarettes using this incident as a real-life example of the dangers they present."

Article continues below

Fire safety teams warn that oxygen can saturate clothes and bedding , meaning a tiny spark can flare up faster and burn hotter than people expect. Patients struggling with cravings can ask staff about nicotine patches, gum or lozenges , which help take the edge off without bringing a vape into an oxygen-rich area.

News.title: Andy Burnham live: PM-in-waiting becomes new Labour leader and vows to "give hope back" to country
News.content:
Andy Burnham will become Labour Party leader today ahead of entering Downing Street on Monday after Keir Starmer announced he was stepping down

Andy Burnham has today been crowned Labour Party leader ahead of becoming PM on Monday - and vowed to give people “hope back” saying he is “ready to lead”.

The Makerfield MP - who only returned to Parliament last month - sailed through uncontested after no other challengers put themselves forward to replace Keir Starmer. Mr Burnham is expected to name his cabinet in the coming days, with Shabana Mahmood widely expected to replace Rachel Reeves as Chancellor.

Mr Burnham was confirmed as Labour leader at a special conference at noon today. He is expected to then make a speech at an event at around 2.30pm, but in the meantime told party members said: “We are united and we put the power that comes from that unity at the service of people and places who have been waiting too long for politics to let them hope again. That’s what we’re going to do, everybody. We’re going to give them hope back.”

In a graceful message to his successor, Mr Starmer said he believes Mr Burnham can win the next general election. He told The Mirror in his final newspaper interview as PM: "There is now I think a sound footing, a sound foundation, and the party can go on and win a second term, which is what I always thought we could do."

Follow our liveblog below for the latest updates..

News.title: Drill rapper jailed for life for stabbing influencer to death while filming music video
News.content:
Drill rapper jailed for life for stabbing influencer to death while filming music video

Ellis Heather, 25, was today handed a life-sentence at the Old Bailey for stabbing content creator Stephen Morrisson, 30, to death at a music video shoot in Epping, Essex

View 2 Images Stephen Morrisson died after being stabbed in Epping (Image: Essex Police)

A drill rapper who murdered a content creator at a music video shoot in Essex has been jailed for life.

‌



Stephen Morrisson, 30, died on June 23, 2020, after suffering a fatal stab injury during a violent assault in a car park in Epping.

‌



Ellis Heather, 25, was today handed a life-sentence at the Old Bailey and must serve a minimum of 28 years.

‌



Stephen, known online as Zero Ls, was stabbed within minutes of stumbling into Heather's music video shoot, during which he was filming with big snakes and a Komodo dragon by the Wake Valley Pond car park, near Loughton.

Heather, whose stage name is Rack5, is a member of CGM - a west London gang also called 1011. He is already serving a prison sentence for firearms offences.

View 2 Images Ellis Heather (Image: Essex Police/PA Wire)

‌



Despite his injuries, Stephen was able to leave the scene and seek help before he tragically died later in hospital.

Heather, formerly of Taplow, Maidenhead, was found guilty of murder by a jury on June 23, 2026, following a five-week trial.

Police trawled through more than 200 hours of CCTV footage and seized mobile phones, almost 40 computer devices and five vehicles during the investigation into Stephen's death.

‌



During the sentencing hearing today, His Honour Judge Lickley KC said Heather was "armed with a knife… and had used it to deadly effect" and that he had "stabbed Stephen without any justification… in a moment of extreme violence".

He then left the scene with no concern for Stephen, the judge added. The Judge also said Heather had boasted about his actions in a music video and had mocked Stephen's family.

In a statement read by Stephen’s mother Lorraine on behalf of her family, she said: "Steve was a son, a brother, a dad and an uncle. Every day we try to keep his memory alive so that his young son, nieces and nephews never forget him, because memories are all we now have left.

‌



"The babies born after his death have been robbed of the chance to know their amazing uncle, because of you. We have attended weddings, family events and celebrations that Steve should have been part of.

"We place a photograph where Steve would have sat so that he is still included. The older children feel the same pain and loss that we do as adults.

"Steve was a huge part of our lives. He was happy, funny and larger than life. His death has left an enormous hole in our family."
